subject: biology
title: Journey Through the Gut
welcome_lead: Follow a bite of apple from your mouth to where it leaves your body.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on the order of digestion through the gut.
final_note: You can now name the digestive organs in the right order from mouth to bottom.

concepts.def: Where food is chewed and mixed with saliva.
Tube carrying food to the stomach.
Bag where food is mixed with acid.
Long tube where nutrients are absorbed.

walkthroughs.body_html: Food travels: mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum. Each part has its own job.
Teeth and saliva start digestion in the mouth. The stomach uses acid to break food. The small intestine absorbs nutrients. The large intestine absorbs water.
Food spends about 1 minute in the oesophagus, 2-4 hours in the stomach, around 4 hours in the small intestine, and up to a day in the large intestine.
